Previous anti-seizure medicines: Levetiracetam (behavioural change, irritability), Carbamazepine (dizziness, hyponatraemia), Valproate (weight gain, tremor), Lamotrigine (ineffective at therapeutic range), Lacosamide (diplopia), Clobazam PRN (sedation), Zonisamide (word-finding difficulty). The app export and in-app graphs were reviewed with the patient during the consultation. According to the log, there were clusters in late 2024, then a progressive reduction in events through spring 2025. - Brivaracetam 100 mg twice daily (initiated March 2025; titrated over 3 weeks)
- Folic acid 5 mg once daily
- Vitamin D3 1000 IU once daily

Adverse effects and wellbeing: Since switching from levetiracetam to brivaracetam, mood and irritability have improved. No new neurological adverse effects reported. - Lifestyle: maintain regular sleep and hydration; no specific restrictions beyond standard safety guidance around water heights and operating at heights.
- Follow-up: routine review in 6 months, sooner if any breakthrough episodes are recorded. We will offer a nurse-led phone check-in in 8–10 weeks to review adherence and diary entries.
